title: Correct public status and projection-shell defects
objective: Make the accepted public documentation and static projection shell accurately describe the live canonical site and current corpus while removing duplicate headings and affordances that overstate lens differentiation.
required_evaluation: live-state claims checked against accepted activation evidence
HTML heading hierarchy and canonical-link tests
desktop and narrow-viewport projection smoke tests
existing deterministic build and disclosure audit
acceptance: README and launch-facing documentation state that the canonical HTTPS site is live while the sharing redirect and hosted API/MCP remain unproved
the homepage honestly identifies the self-describing bootstrap corpus until an external dossier is accepted
default topic pages contain one top-level heading rather than a duplicated title and description
public lens affordances do not imply material policy divergence that the compiler does not implement
canonical URLs, Markdown twins, object routes, manifests, and machine interfaces retain their identities and expected content types
make check passes without changing accepted source state
limitations: This task does not redesign the visual system, introduce an external dossier, change protocol schemas or policies, activate episte.media, or deploy API/MCP.
Correct status prose is provider-read-back documentation, not a claim that every planned public service is live.
